verdict.rationale: Zapier documents a developer platform where outside parties build integrations with the Visual Builder or the Platform CLI and publish them to the App Directory. Partner integration versions follow a documented lifecycle, so the core of the story exists. The consumer side is only implied: the pack never explicitly describes users discovering or installing these partner-built integrations. missing for 10: explicit documentation of users installing or enabling third-party-published integrations, evidence of truly community (non-app-vendor) contributions, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can install community-built nodes, components, or integrations contributed outside the vendor

citations.quote: Build a Zapier integration - design triggers and actions for your product, wire up authentication, then publish to the App Directory.
Zapier Platform CLI enables developers to build integrations using Node.js v22, OAuth1/OAuth2 authentication, webhooks, polling triggers, and HTTP middleware.
This lifecycle governs partner integration versions
ZPS is a separate free account workspace for partners with a beta or public integration
